name: CrewPoppy
description: The HQ for your AI crew — task-specific AI agents that run entirely in your own AWS, with hard spend caps and every action visible.

permissionSet.name: CrewPoppy backend
permissionSet.description: Deploys and removes its own CloudFormation stack (CrewPoppyStack): the agents table, the agent workspace bucket, the agent-runner function and its execution role. Every change and delete is limited to resources named CrewPoppy*/crewpoppy-* — it cannot touch anything else in your account. The one role it creates is the runner's own, name-locked to CrewPoppy*, and only that role can invoke AI models (Bedrock) — billed to your AWS, capped by CrewPoppy's spend limits. If you let an agent send email, that role can also send from addresses you have ALREADY verified in SES — it can never verify a new one, and CrewPoppy refuses to send to anyone but you until you approve that exact message. Here it only READS whether an address is verified. For the phone app it also creates one Cognito sign-in pool holding a single user — you — with no self-signup: only pairing from this desktop can create or reset that login, and removing CrewPoppy deletes the pool.

grants.reason: The stack's own execution roles, name-locked to CrewPoppy*. The two boundary actions CAP those roles rather than grant them anything: CloudFormation attaches AgentsPoppy's ceiling policy when the account has one, and removes it again if that is ever turned off. Both are needed — an existing role gains its boundary by Put, and loses it by Delete.
Checks whether an AI model is switched on in your account before offering it to you, so a missing one is caught at setup instead of mid-run. It never sees a prompt or an answer.
Checks that the sender address you chose is verified with AWS before an agent sends from it. It cannot send mail, and it cannot change any mail setting.

The mobile app's login (P4): one user pool holding ONE user — the owner. Pool ids are generated, so creates can't be name-scoped narrower. Tag/UntagResource are how CloudFormation's own Cognito handler applies the attribution tags: it creates the pool, then tags it in a SEPARATE call (live failure 2026-07-30 — without TagResource the deploy rolls back on AccessDenied).
Managing that same pool and its single owner account — only on pools CrewPoppy itself created (tag-enforced), incl. teardown.

compliance.dataHandled: Agent prompts, memory, outputs and spend records, stored only in your own AWS account; model calls run on Amazon Bedrock inside your account. Where you direct an agent to reach an external service, that destination is your choice, made visibly.
